concepts.title: Plane Angle
concepts.definition: The length's ratio of a circular arc to the radius of that circle, representing angular span in a two-dimensional plane.
concepts.key_idea: Plane angle is measured in radians and is a dimensionless quantity.

solution_steps.action: divide arc length by radius
solution_steps.explain: The plane angle is the ratio of the arc length to the radius of the circle.

solution_steps.action: convert the angle from radians to degrees if required
solution_steps.explain: Since 1 radian equals 180/pi degrees, multiply by 180/pi to express the angle in degrees.

solution_steps.action: round the result to the appropriate significant figures
solution_steps.explain: The plane angle is dimensionless, so round the final value to match the significant figures of the given arc length and radius.

concepts.title: Dimensional Consistency of Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: Verifying if a proposed formula for kinetic energy is dimensionally correct by comparing its dimensions with those of energy, which are [M L^2 T^-2].
concepts.key_idea: Only formulas whose terms simplify to the dimensions of energy are physically valid representations of kinetic energy.
question_patterns: check if the formula for kinetic energy is dimensionally correct
verify the dimensional consistency of kinetic energy equations
which of the following formulas for kinetic energy are dimensionally valid
determine if the equation for kinetic energy is dimensionally homogeneous
why is dimensional consistency of kinetic energy important

solution_steps.action: Determine the dimensions of the left-hand side (kinetic energy).
solution_steps.explain: Kinetic energy has the dimensions of work or energy, which is [M L^2 T^-2].

solution_steps.action: Determine the dimensions of each term on the right-hand side.
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the dimensions of mass [M], velocity [L T^-1], and acceleration [L T^-2] into the given expression.

solution_steps.action: Compare the dimensions of both sides.
solution_steps.explain: If the dimensions of the right-hand side match [M L^2 T^-2], the formula is dimensionally correct.
